## 1. `TerminalStatusBar.swift` — Investigate call site

private var diagnosis: AgentBannerState? { state == nil ? nil : agentManager.banners[tabID] }

Full function (`Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:297-338`):

```swift

    let tint = diagnosisTint(model.style)

      showingDiagnosis.toggle()

## 2. `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — Investigate call site

Full function (`Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:428-455`):

```swift
/// The ✦ agent popover for a tab (inline presentation): the diagnosis + its actions, off the grid.
@ViewBuilder private func agentPopover(for tab: TerminalTab) -> some View {
    if let state = agentManager.banners[tab.id] {
      TerminalAgentBanner(
        state: state,
        onDiagnose: { agentManager.diagnose(tab: tab.id, target: target.id) },
        onInsertFix: { fix in
          if case .terminal(let s) = tab.content { s.view.sendText(fix) }
          agentPopoverTab = nil
        },
        onInvestigate: {
          let cwd: String
          if case .terminal(let s) = tab.content {
            cwd = s.view.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
          } else {
            cwd = target.path
          }
          _ = store.terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: "claude", cwd: cwd)
          agentManager.dismiss(tab: tab.id)
          agentPopoverTab = nil
        },
        onDismiss: {
          agentManager.dismiss(tab: tab.id)
          agentPopoverTab = nil
        }
      )
      .frame(width: 360)
    }
  }
```

- `target` is a stored property (`Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:20`, `let target: TerminalTarget`).
- `cwd` is derived per-tab from `tab.content` matched against `.terminal` — a third, slightly different derivation from the StatusBar's.
- **`AgentBannerState` IS available right here**, bound as `state` in the enclosing `if let state = agentManager.banners[tab.id]` (line 429) and passed straight into `TerminalAgentBanner(state: state, ...)`. The `onInvestigate` closure simply never uses it — it hardcodes the literal `"claude"` instead of calling `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: state)`. This is the single easiest fix in the whole issue.
- Uses `store.terminals.addRunTab` where `store: AppStore` is `@EnvironmentObject` (line 22) and `sessions`/`terminals` is `@ObservedObject var sessions: TerminalSessions` (line 21) — both views have equal access to `store`, so both could route through `AppStore` bookkeeping.

## 3. `TerminalSessions.swift` — `addRunTab`

Doc comment + signature (`Core/TerminalSessions.swift:945-987`):

```swift
/// Open the dedicated "run command" terminal (issue #7): a solo tab that launches `command` in
/// `cwd`, titled "Run" until the program reports its own title, focused like any new tab — through
/// `setFocused`, so focus observers fire (it is NOT a direct dict write; see the focus-chokepoint
/// note on `setFocused`). The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires `onChildExited`;
/// this just creates and shows the tab.
///
/// Run-tab lifecycle — one `AppStore.RunState` per target; the pane stays open on exit via
/// `wait_after_command`:
/// ```
///   armed                       auto-run queued before the workroom's pane exists; consumed on mount
///   start (no state / armed) ─▶ spawn surface (command = $SHELL -lic '<cmd>', wait_after_command);
///                               focus; state = running
///
///   running ──────── Run / ⌘R ─────────▶ focus (no respawn)
///   running ──────── Stop (1st) ───────▶ Ctrl-C; state = running(interrupted)
///   running ──────── Restart ──────────▶ Ctrl-C; state = restarting
///   running / running(interrupted) ── child exits ─▶ stopped (pane open)
///   running(interrupted) ── Stop (2nd) ─▶ closeTab → ghostty_surface_free (SIGHUP, hard kill)
///   restarting ── child exits ─▶ close + respawn (graceful; frees the port); Stop ─▶ running(interrupted)
///   stopped ──────── Run / ⌘R / Restart ─▶ close + respawn
///   any state ────── close tab (⌘W/✕) / reap ─▶ removed (state cleared via onTabsRemoved)
/// ```
/// A backgrounded run tab is never the active tab, so it never mounts — and a libghostty surface
/// spawns its process only on window-mount. We give the off-window `ensureSurfaceCreated` a sane
/// initial size so the command starts with reasonable COLUMNS/LINES; it re-sizes on first real mount.
static let backgroundRunInitialSize = CGSize(width: 800, height: 480)

@discardableResult
func addRunTab(for target: TerminalTarget, command: String, cwd: String, focus: Bool = true)
  -> TerminalTab
{
  let tab = makeRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
  insert(tab, for: target)
  if focus {
    setFocused(tab.id, for: target.id)
  } else {
    tab.surface?.ensureSurfaceCreated(initialSize: Self.backgroundRunInitialSize)
  }
  reconcileOcclusion(for: target)
  return tab
}
```

The load-bearing line: **"The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires `onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab."** `respawnRunTab`'s doc echoes it (`Core/TerminalSessions.swift:995`): "Returns the new tab so the caller wires run-state + `onChildExited`, as `addRunTab` does." Neither Investigate call site is that caller — both call `addRunTab` directly from a View, bypassing `AppStore` entirely.

## 4. `AppStore.swift`

**`startRunCommand`** (`Core/AppStore.swift:1916-1962`):

```swift
/// Start the project's run command in `target`'s directory, in a dedicated run terminal. No-op
/// without a configured command or for a missing target. One run terminal per target (a second start
/// is a no-op, not a duplicate).
///
/// Issue #67: the run starts in the BACKGROUND by default — `focus` is false, so it doesn't steal the
/// foreground tab; a toast surfaces its status. `focus: true` is only for auto-run on a freshly
/// created workroom where the run would be the sole tab (Arch #5) — there we DO show it.
func startRunCommand(for target: TerminalTarget, focus: Bool = false) {
  guard !target.isMissing, let project = project(forTarget: target) else { return }
  let config = runConfig(forProject: project.path)
  guard config.hasCommand else { return }
  if let existing = runStates[target.id]?.tab {
    // issue #67: a plain start never steals focus — only the auto-run-only-tab case passes focus.
    if focus { terminals.focus(existing, for: target) }
    return
  }
  let pidPath = makeRunPidPath()
  let line = runCommandLine(
    config.command.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines), pidPath: pidPath)
  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: line, cwd: target.path, focus: focus)
  runOutcomes[target.id] = nil  // a fresh run clears the prior outcome (issue #67)
  resetRunToast(for: target.id)  // a new run always gets a fresh toast (clear dismiss + timer)
  if !focus, tab.surface?.didSpawnFail == true {
    runOutcomes[target.id] = .failedToStart
    runStates[target.id] = .stopped(tab: tab.id)
    scheduleRunToastAutoDismiss(for: target.id)
    postRunFailureBannerIfBackgrounded(
      targetID: target.id, tabID: tab.id, title: "Run failed to start",
      body: config.command.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines))
    return
  }
  runStates[target.id] = .running(tab: tab.id, interrupted: false)
  runPidFiles[target.id] = pidPath  // after the tab exists, so cleanup can't wipe it
  lastRunStatus[target.id] = nil
  captureRunSession(for: target.id, pidPath: pidPath)
  pollRunStatus(for: target)  // status file drives state from here (issue #7)
  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] code in
    self?.markRunExited(for: target, exitCode: code)
  }
  wireRunClose(tab.id, for: target)
}
```

**Key constraint for the plan: `startRunCommand` guards on `config.hasCommand` and short-circuits to the existing tab when `runStates[target.id]?.tab != nil`.** It is written for exactly one run per target, not "run any command." Investigate can't just call `startRunCommand` as-is — it needs either its own analogous bookkeeping path or `RunState`/the run bookkeeping needs to become keyed differently (see below).

**`runStates` + `RunState`** (`Core/AppStore.swift:1310-1342, 1368-1371`):

```swift
/// The lifecycle of a target's run command (issue #7), one value per target. A single state machine
/// replaces the former parallel sets/maps — every transition is explicit...
enum RunState: Equatable {
  case armed
  case running(tab: TerminalTab.ID, interrupted: Bool)
  case restarting(tab: TerminalTab.ID)
  case stopped(tab: TerminalTab.ID)

  var tab: TerminalTab.ID? {
    switch self {
    case .running(let tab, _), .restarting(let tab), .stopped(let tab): return tab
    case .armed: return nil
    }
  }
  var isRunning: Bool {
    switch self {
    case .running, .restarting: return true
    case .armed, .stopped: return false
    }
  }
}
...
/// Run-STATE is owned here (not on `TerminalSessions`) so the toolbar, sidebar, menu, and RootView
/// — which all observe this store — react to start/stop/exit from one `@Published` source (OV-A).
/// `TerminalSessions` only creates/focuses the tab and reports its removal via `onTabsRemoved`.
@Published private(set) var runStates: [TerminalTarget.ID: RunState] = [:]
```

**`runStates` is keyed by `TerminalTarget.ID`, one `RunState` per target** — not per tab, not per project. This is the central fork the plan must resolve: an Investigate session is conceptually a second, independent "run" in the same target that may already have its own dev-server `RunState` occupying that slot. `RunState` has no room for a second tab per target as written.

**`liveRunView` / `hasLiveRunCommand`** (`Core/AppStore.swift:2246-2259`):

```swift
/// The target's run surface if a child process is still alive in it, else nil. Used by the
/// teardown paths to decide whether a Ctrl-C + wait is needed before freeing it.
private func liveRunView(for targetID: TerminalTarget.ID) -> GhosttySurfaceView? {
  guard let tabID = runStates[targetID]?.tab,
    let view = terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID),
    view.hasLiveProcess
  else { return nil }
  return view
}

/// Whether any run command still has a live process — gates the quit handler's graceful wait.
var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
}
```

Both derive strictly from `runStates`, so any tab not registered there is invisible to teardown.

**`onChildExited` wiring for run commands** — two sites, both in `AppStore`, both only reachable through the "owning" start paths:
- `startRunCommand`: `Core/AppStore.swift:1958-1960`
- `respawnRunCommand` (the in-place restart): `Core/AppStore.swift:2016-2018`

```swift
tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] code in
  self?.markRunExited(for: target, exitCode: code)
}
```

Neither Investigate call site wires this. `Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:69` declares the property (`var onChildExited: ((UInt32) -> Void)?`), and `:724` fires it — an Investigate tab's `claude` process exiting fires nothing.

## 5. `WindowRegistry.swift` — `runOwner`

Full body (`Core/WindowRegistry.swift:205-212`):

```swift
// MARK: Run-command ownership

/// The other window already running `target`'s run command, if any. Derived from each window's live
/// `runStates` (no separate map to drift): a second window's Run focuses this owner instead of
/// forking a duplicate dev server on the same port (issue #70 / issue #7).
func runOwner(for target: TerminalTarget.ID, excluding: AppStore) -> AppStore? {
  allStores.first { $0 !== excluding && ($0.runStates[target]?.isRunning ?? false) }
}
```

Callers:
- `Core/AppStore.swift:2113` — inside `runOrFocusRunCommand(for:)`, the toolbar Run/⌘R handler: when no run state exists locally, checks whether another window already owns the target's run command and focuses that window instead of starting a duplicate.
- Documented (not called) in `Core/SessionSnapshot.swift:36` and `Views/TargetDetailToolbar.swift:130` as the mechanism that prevents a second dev server on the same port.

This is single-owner, cross-window dedup logic keyed on `runStates[target].isRunning` — another reason `runStates` can't trivially gain a second "always concurrent" per-target entry for Investigate without touching this too (an Investigate `claude` session should almost certainly NOT be deduped/redirected across windows the way a dev server is).

## 6. `AgentPrompt` / `AgentBannerState`

`AgentPrompt` lives at `Core/AgentPrompt.swift`. Relevant definitions:

```swift
// Core/AgentPrompt.swift:56-61
/// A shell command line that opens an interactive `claude` seeded with the failure so the agent can
/// start investigating immediately (issue #49). Run in the pane's real cwd (unlike the neutral-dir
/// no-tools diagnosis), so it can inspect the project.
static func investigateCommandLine(for state: AgentBannerState) -> String {
  let (failure, diagnosis) = state.failureAndDiagnosis
  let prompt = investigatePrompt(
    command: failure.command, exitCode: failure.exitCode, diagnosis: diagnosis)
  return "claude " + shellSingleQuoted(prompt)
}

// Core/AgentPrompt.swift:63-83
/// The natural-language seed prompt for the interactive Investigate session: the failed command,
/// its exit code, and (when available) the quick diagnosis, then an instruction to dig in. Output
/// is deliberately omitted — the agent runs in the real cwd and can re-run the command itself.
static func investigatePrompt(command: String?, exitCode: Int32, diagnosis: AgentDiagnosis?)
  -> String
{
  var lines: [String] = []
  if let command = nonBlank(command) {
    lines.append("I ran `\(command)` in this directory and it failed with exit code \(exitCode).")
  } else {
    lines.append("A command in this directory failed with exit code \(exitCode).")
  }
  if let diagnosis {
    lines.append("A quick automated check suggested this cause: \(diagnosis.summary)")
    if let fix = nonBlank(diagnosis.fixCommand) {
      lines.append("and this unverified fix: \(fix)")
    }
  }
  lines.append("Please investigate the root cause and help me fix it.")
  return lines.joined(separator: "\n")
}
```

`AgentBannerState` is defined in `Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:29-53`, alongside the `FailedCommand` it wraps:

```swift
// Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:8-16
struct FailedCommand: Equatable, Sendable {
  var command: String?
  var cwd: String?
  var exitCode: Int32
  var shell: String?
  var output: String
  var isRunTab: Bool
  var isRemote: Bool
}

// Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:29-53
/// What the banner shows for a tab (issue #49). Absent (no entry) means no banner.
enum AgentBannerState: Equatable, Sendable {
  case awaitingDiagnose(FailedCommand)
  case loading(FailedCommand)
  case ready(FailedCommand, AgentDiagnosis)
  case failure(FailedCommand, AgentErrorKind)
  case remoteCaveat(FailedCommand)

  var failureAndDiagnosis: (FailedCommand, AgentDiagnosis?) {
    switch self {
    case .awaitingDiagnose(let failure), .loading(let failure), .failure(let failure, _),
      .remoteCaveat(let failure):
      return (failure, nil)
    case .ready(let failure, let diagnosis):
      return (failure, diagnosis)
    }
  }
}
```

Note `FailedCommand.cwd` — the banner state already carries a `cwd` captured at failure time (`Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:6`: "The host builds this from the surface view (command + cwd from shell integration...)"), a fourth possible cwd source neither call site currently reads; both instead re-derive cwd live from the surface/target at Investigate time.

## 8. Quit-time graceful teardown — what "waits for" a run command

Chain from `hasLiveRunCommand`/`liveRunView` up to the app-quit and window-close paths:

**Per-store gate** (`Core/AppStore.swift:2246-2259`, shown above) — `hasLiveRunCommand` is true only if `runStates[targetID]?.tab` exists AND that tab's surface `hasLiveProcess`.

**Cross-window aggregation** (`Core/WindowRegistry.swift:216-234`):

```swift
/// Any window with a live run command — gates the graceful-stop-on-quit (issue #7 / #70).
var hasAnyLiveRunCommand: Bool { allStores.contains(where: \.hasLiveRunCommand) }

/// Ctrl-C every window's live run commands and let them exit before the process dies...
func gracefullyStopAllWindows(timeout: TimeInterval, completion: @escaping () -> Void) {
  let live = allStores.filter(\.hasLiveRunCommand)
  guard !live.isEmpty else {
    completion()
    return
  }
  let group = DispatchGroup()
  for store in live {
    group.enter()
    store.gracefullyStopAllRunCommands(timeout: timeout) { group.leave() }
  }
  group.notify(queue: .main) { completion() }
}
```

**App-quit call site** (`WorkroomApp.swift:627-646`, `stopRunCommandsThenTerminate`, called from `applicationShouldTerminate` at line 619):

```swift
private func stopRunCommandsThenTerminate(_ sender: NSApplication) -> NSApplication.TerminateReply {
  let registry = WindowRegistry.shared
  registry.isTerminating = true
  SessionCoordinator.shared.flushAndFreeze()
  guard registry.hasAnyLiveRunCommand else { return .terminateNow }
  registry.gracefullyStopAllWindows(timeout: 5) {
    sender.reply(toApplicationShouldTerminate: true)
  }
  return .terminateLater
}
```

**SIGTERM path** (`WorkroomApp.swift:507-524`, `installSigtermHandler`) — same `gracefullyStopAllWindows` call, timeout 4s, then `exit(EXIT_SUCCESS)`.

**Per-window close** (`Core/WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`, `WindowCloseGuard.windowShouldClose`):

```swift
func windowShouldClose(_ sender: NSWindow) -> Bool {
  MainActor.assumeIsolated {
    guard let store, !WindowRegistry.shared.isTerminating, store.hasLiveRunCommand else {
      return true
    }
    if Defaults[.confirmOnQuit] {
      let alert = NSAlert()
      alert.messageText = "Close this window?"
      alert.informativeText = "It has a running process. Closing the window will stop it."
      alert.addButton(withTitle: "Close")
      alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
      guard alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn else { return false }
    }
    store.gracefullyStopAllRunCommands(timeout: 5) { sender.close() }
    return false
  }
}
```

**Per-tab close** (`Core/AppStore.swift:2338-2346`, `closingRunTab`, gates ⌘W / tab-close on a run tab):

```swift
let isRunTab = runStates[targetID]?.tab == tabID
let live = liveRunView(for: targetID) != nil
guard isRunTab, live else {
  proceed()  // not a live run tab → free directly (no supervisor to gracefully stop)
  return
}
gracefullyStopRuns([targetID], then: proceed)
```

### Consequence chain for an unregistered Investigate tab

Because neither Investigate call site touches `runStates`, an Investigate tab is invisible to every one of the above checks:

# Fix issue #146 — Investigate's untracked agent + diverging call sites

## Context

Issue #146 found two bugs in the "Investigate" button (issue #49), which opens an interactive
`claude` session seeded with a failed command's context. It has two call sites —
`TerminalStatusBar.swift` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — and both call
`TerminalSessions.addRunTab` directly instead of going through `AppStore`, which violates
`addRunTab`'s own documented contract ("The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab.").

**Bug 1 (low severity):** because neither call site registers with `AppStore.runStates`, the
spawned agent is invisible to `hasLiveRunCommand`. Quit and window-close teardown never notice
it's alive — a live Investigate conversation gets silently SIGHUP'd instead of getting the same
"still running, are you sure?" treatment a run command gets. The issue's own severity note is
right that there's no port to leak, but silently killing an interactive session mid-conversation
is still a real (if minor) UX gap.

**Bug 2 (medium severity, user-visible):** the tab-strip call site hardcodes the literal
`"claude"` instead of building the seeded prompt via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`
the way the status-bar site does. Opening Investigate from the tab-strip popover throws away the
whole point of the feature — the agent starts with no idea what failed.

The chosen fix (confirmed with the user): don't widen `RunState`/`runStates` — that model is one
value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.

## Changes

### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point

Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
`RunState`:

```swift
/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
/// SIGHUP'ing it.
@Published private(set) var investigateTabs: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTarget.ID] = [:]
```

Near `startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:~1916`), add the single entry point
both views will call:

```swift
/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
@discardableResult
func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
  -> TerminalTab
{
  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
  }
  return tab
}
```

Update `hasLiveRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:2257`) to also check live Investigate tabs, reusing
the same `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` pattern `liveRunView` already uses:

```swift
var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
    }
}
```

In the `onTabsRemoved` closure (`AppStore.swift:916-941`), which already clears `runStates` when
its tab is closed/reaped, add the equivalent purge for `investigateTabs` so a closed tab's entry
doesn't linger:

```swift
ids.forEach { self.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: $0) }
```

Do **not** touch `gracefullyStopRuns`/`gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` — they SIGTERM a target's
run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session
has none of. `hasLiveRunCommand` going true is what makes `windowShouldClose`'s confirm-on-close
alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the
process on confirm is just the surface's normal teardown, same as closing any terminal tab.

### 2. `TerminalStatusBar.swift:326-332` — route through the new method

Replace the direct `addRunTab` call in the `onInvestigate` closure:

```swift
onInvestigate: {
  let cwd = state?.view.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: bannerState, target: target, cwd: cwd)
  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tabID)
  showingDiagnosis = false
},
```

(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here.)

### 3. `TerminalTabStrip.swift:436-441` — fix bug 2 and route through the new method

Replace the hardcoded `"claude"` + direct `addRunTab` call:

```swift
onInvestigate: {
  let cwd: String
  if case .terminal(let s) = tab.content {
    cwd = s.view.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
  } else {
    cwd = target.path
  }
  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: state, target: target, cwd: cwd)
  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tab.id)
  agentPopoverTab = nil
},
```

(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here; `state` is the `AgentBannerState`
already bound by the enclosing `if let state = agentManager.banners[tab.id]`.)

This fixes bug 2 (both sites now build the identical seeded command via
`AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`) and closes bug 1 (both sites now go through
`AppStore`, which owns the tracking, restoring `addRunTab`'s documented caller contract).

### 4. `TerminalSessions.swift:945-952` — doc note

Add one line to `addRunTab`'s doc comment noting Investigate sessions are tracked in
`AppStore.investigateTabs`, not `runStates`, so the split is explicit at the definition too (not
just at the call sites) — closes the issue's "or a comment explaining why" fallback for the part
that *is* staying a deliberate design choice (no cross-window dedup, no supervisor/pidfile).

## Verification

- `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests.swift` — add:
  - A test asserting `startInvestigate` produces a tab whose command matches
    `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` for a given `AgentBannerState`, and that
    `investigateTabs[tab.id] == target.id` afterward — covers "both call sites build the same
    command line" (the issue's suggested unit check) by construction, since both now call the
    one method.
  - A test that `hasLiveRunCommand` is `false` before `startInvestigate`, `true` while the tab's
    surface reports a live process, and `false` again after simulating `onChildExited` and after
    simulating tab removal (mirrors the existing `testGracefullyStopAllWaitsForEveryLiveCommandThenCompletes`
    / `testReapClearsRunState` style already in this file).
- `make app-lint` / `make app-format` on the touched files.
- `make app-test` (or scoped `xcodebuild -only-testing:WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests`) green.
- Manual, per the issue's own verification section:
  - Fail a command, open Investigate from the status bar and from the tab-strip chip — confirm
    both agents start with the failure context (the prompt text, not a bare `claude`).
  - Start Investigate, then ⌘Q / close the window with "confirm on quit" enabled — confirm the
    close-confirmation now accounts for the live agent instead of silently killing it.

3. **The recommendation and why** — a `Recommendation: <choice> because <reason>` line plus the `(recommended)` marker on that choice.

Layout: a `D<N>` title + a one-line note to reply with a letter (in Conductor this is the normal path; elsewhere it means AskUserQuestion was unavailable or errored); the issue ELI10; the Recommendation line; then ONE paragraph per choice carrying its `(recommended)` marker, its `Completeness: X/10`, and 2-4 sentences of reasoning — never a bare bullet list; a closing `Net:` line. Split chains / 5+ options: one prose block per per-option call, in sequence. Then STOP and wait — the user's typed answer is the decision. In plan mode this satisfies end-of-turn like a tool call.

**Continuation — mapping a typed reply back to a brief.** Each brief carries a stable label (`D<N>`, or `D<N>.k` in a split chain). The user references it (e.g. "3.2: B"). A bare letter maps to the single most-recent UNANSWERED brief; if more than one is open (a split chain), do NOT guess — ask which `D<N>.k` it answers. Never apply a bare letter ambiguously across a chain.

**One-way / destructive confirmations in prose.** When the decision is a one-way door (irreversible or destructive — delete, force-push, drop, overwrite), prose is a WEAKER gate than the tool, so make it stronger: require an explicit typed confirmation (the exact option letter or word), state plainly what is irreversible, and NEVER proceed on a vague, partial, or ambiguous reply — re-ask instead. Treat silence or "ok"/"sure" without the explicit choice as not-yet-confirmed.

### Format

Every AskUserQuestion is a decision brief and must be sent as tool_use, not prose — unless the documented failure fallback above applies (interactive session + the call is unavailable/erroring), in which case the prose fallback is the correct output.

```
D<N> — <one-line question title>
Project/branch/task: <1 short grounding sentence using _BRANCH>
ELI10: <plain English a 16-year-old could follow, 2-4 sentences, name the stakes>
Stakes if we pick wrong: <one sentence on what breaks, what user sees, what's lost>
Recommendation: <choice> because <one-line reason>
Completeness: A=X/10, B=Y/10   (or: Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score)
Pros / cons:
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)

      echo "semantic questions; use \`gbrain code-def\`/\`code-refs\`/\`code-callers\` for"
      echo "symbol-aware code lookup. See \"## GBrain Search Guidance\" in CLAUDE.md."
      echo "Run /sync-gbrain to refresh."
    else

      echo "before relying on \`gbrain search\` for code questions in this worktree."
      echo "Falls back to Grep until pinned."
    fi
  fi
fi

_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$("$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN" get artifacts_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)

# Detect remote-MCP mode (Path 4 of /setup-gbrain). Local artifacts sync is
# a no-op in remote mode; the brain server pulls from GitHub/GitLab on its
# own cadence. Read claude.json directly to keep this preamble fast (no
# subprocess to claude CLI on every skill start).
_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="none"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$HOME/.claude.json" ]; then
  _GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.type // .mcpServers.gbrain.transport // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$_GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE" in
    url|http|sse) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="remote-http" ;;
    stdio) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="local-stdio" ;;
  esac
fi

if [ -f "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" ] && [ ! -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" = "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_NEW_URL=$(head -1 "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')

if [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then

    _BRAIN_AGE=$(( _BRAIN_NOW - _BRAIN_LAST ))

## Model-Specific Behavioral Patch (claude)

The following nudges are tuned for the claude model family. They are
**subordinate** to skill workflow, STOP points, AskUserQuestion gates, plan-mode
safety, and /ship review gates. If a nudge below conflicts with skill instructions,
the skill wins. Treat these as preferences, not rules.

**Todo-list discipline.** When working through a multi-step plan, mark each task
complete individually as you finish it. Do not batch-complete at the end. If a task
turns out to be unnecessary, mark it skipped with a one-line reason.

**Think before heavy actions.** For complex operations (refactors, migrations,
non-trivial new features), briefly state your approach before executing. This lets
the user course-correct cheaply instead of mid-flight.

**Dedicated tools over Bash.** Prefer Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep over shell
equivalents (cat, sed, find, grep). The dedicated tools are cheaper and clearer.

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.
- Be concrete. Name files, functions, line numbers, commands, outputs, evals, and real numbers.
- Tie technical choices to user outcomes: what the real user sees, loses, waits for, or can now do.
- Be direct about quality. Bugs matter. Edge cases matter. Fix the whole thing, not the demo path.
- Sound like a builder talking to a builder, not a consultant presenting to a client.
- Never corporate, academic, PR, or hype. Avoid filler, throat-clearing, generic optimism, and founder cosplay.
- No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted, furthermore, moreover, additionally, pivotal, landscape, tapestry, underscore, foster, showcase, intricate, vibrant, fundamental, significant.
- The user has context you do not: domain knowledge, timing, relationships, taste. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.

Good: "auth.ts:47 returns undefined when the session cookie expires. Users hit a white screen. Fix: add a null check and redirect to /login. Two lines."
Bad: "I've identified a potential issue in the authentication flow that may cause problems under certain conditions."

## Writing Style (skip entirely if `EXPLAIN_LEVEL: terse` appears in the preamble echo OR the user's current message explicitly requests terse / no-explanations output)

Applies to AskUserQuestion, user replies, and findings. AskUserQuestion Format is structure; this is prose quality.

- Gloss curated jargon on first use per skill invocation, even if the user pasted the term.
- Frame questions in outcome terms: what pain is avoided, what capability unlocks, what user experience changes.
- Use short sentences, concrete nouns, active voice.
- Close decisions with user impact: what the user sees, waits for, loses, or gains.
- User-turn override wins: if the current message asks for terse / no explanations / just the answer, skip this section.
- Terse mode (EXPLAIN_LEVEL: terse): no glosses, no outcome-framing layer, shorter responses.

Curated jargon list lives at `~/.claude/skills/gstack/scripts/jargon-list.json` (80+ terms). On the first jargon term you encounter this session, Read that file once; treat the `terms` array as the canonical list. The list is repo-owned and may grow between releases.


## Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean

AI makes completeness cheap, so the complete thing is the goal. Recommend full coverage (tests, edge cases, error paths) — boil the ocean one lake at a time. The only thing out of scope is genuinely unrelated work (rewrites, multi-quarter migrations); flag that as separate scope, never as an excuse for a shortcut.

When options differ in coverage, include `Completeness: X/10` (10 = all edge cases, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut). When options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.` Do not fabricate scores.

## Confusion Protocol

For high-stakes ambiguity (architecture, data model, destructive scope, missing context), STOP. Name it in one sentence, present 2-3 options with tradeoffs, and ask. Do not use for routine coding or obvious changes.

## Continuous Checkpoint Mode

If `CHECKPOINT_MODE` is `"continuous"`: auto-commit completed logical units with `WIP:` prefix.

Commit after new intentional files, completed functions/modules, verified bug fixes, and before long-running install/build/test commands.

Commit format:

```
WIP: <concise description of what changed>

[gstack-context]
Decisions: <key choices made this step>
Remaining: <what's left in the logical unit>

## Question Tuning (skip entirely if `QUESTION_TUNING: false`)

Before each AskUserQuestion, choose `question_id` from `scripts/question-registry.ts` or `{skill}-{slug}`, then run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-question-preference --check "<id>"`. `AUTO_DECIDE` means choose the recommended option and say "Auto-decided [summary] → [option] (your preference). Change with /plan-tune." `ASK_NORMALLY` means ask.

**Embed the question_id as a marker in the question text** so hooks can identify it deterministically (plan-tune cathedral T14 / D18 progressive markers). Append `<gstack-qid:{question_id}>` somewhere in the rendered question (the leading line or trailing line is fine; the marker doesn't render visibly to the user when wrapped in HTML-style angle brackets, but the hook strips it). Without the marker the PreToolUse enforcement hook treats the AUQ as observed-only and never auto-decides — so always include it when the question matches a registered `question_id`.

**Embed the option recommendation via the `(recommended)` label suffix** on exactly one option per AUQ. The PreToolUse hook parses `(recommended)` first, falls back to "Recommendation: X" prose, and refuses to auto-decide if ambiguous. Two `(recommended)` labels = refuse.

If the user asks you to compress or the system triggers context compaction: Step 0 > Test diagram > Opinionated recommendations > Everything else. Never skip Step 0 or the test diagram. Do not preemptively warn about context limits -- the system handles compaction automatically.

## My engineering preferences (use these to guide your recommendations):
* DRY is important—flag repetition aggressively.
* Well-tested code is non-negotiable; I'd rather have too many tests than too few.
* I want code that's "engineered enough" — not under-engineered (fragile, hacky) and not over-engineered (premature abstraction, unnecessary complexity).
* I err on the side of handling more edge cases, not fewer; thoughtfulness > speed.
* Bias toward explicit over clever.
* Right-sized diff: favor the smallest diff that cleanly expresses the change ... but don't compress a necessary rewrite into a minimal patch. If the existing foundation is broken, say "scrap it and do this instead."

## Cognitive Patterns — How Great Eng Managers Think

These are not additional checklist items. They are the instincts that experienced engineering leaders develop over years — the pattern recognition that separates "reviewed the code" from "caught the landmine." Apply them throughout your review.

1. **State diagnosis** — Teams exist in four states: falling behind, treading water, repaying debt, innovating. Each demands a different intervention (Larson, An Elegant Puzzle).
2. **Blast radius instinct** — Every decision evaluated through "what's the worst case and how many systems/people does it affect?"
3. **Boring by default** — "Every company gets about three innovation tokens." Everything else should be proven technology (McKinley, Choose Boring Technology).
4. **Incremental over revolutionary** — Strangler fig, not big bang. Canary, not global rollout. Refactor, not rewrite (Fowler).
5. **Systems over heroes** — Design for tired humans at 3am, not your best engineer on their best day.
6. **Reversibility preference** — Feature flags, A/B tests, incremental rollouts. Make the cost of being wrong low.
7. **Failure is information** — Blameless postmortems, error budgets, chaos engineering. Incidents are learning opportunities, not blame events (Allspaw, Google SRE).
8. **Org structure IS architecture** — Conway's Law in practice. Design both intentionally (Skelton/Pais, Team Topologies).
9. **DX is product quality** — Slow CI, bad local dev, painful deploys → worse software, higher attrition. Developer experience is a leading indicator.
10. **Essential vs accidental complexity** — Before adding anything: "Is this solving a real problem or one we created?" (Brooks, No Silver Bullet).
11. **Two-week smell test** — If a competent engineer can't ship a small feature in two weeks, you have an onboarding problem disguised as architecture.
12. **Glue work awareness** — Recognize invisible coordination work. Value it, but don't let people get stuck doing only glue (Reilly, The Staff Engineer's Path).
13. **Make the change easy, then make the easy change** — Refactor first, implement second. Never structural + behavioral changes simultaneously (Beck).
14. **Own your code in production** — No wall between dev and ops. "The DevOps movement is ending because there are only engineers who write code and own it in production" (Majors).
15. **Error budgets over uptime targets** — SLO of 99.9% = 0.1% downtime *budget to spend on shipping*. Reliability is resource allocation (Google SRE).

When evaluating architecture, think "boring by default." When reviewing tests, think "systems over heroes." When assessing complexity, ask Brooks's question. When a plan introduces new infrastructure, check whether it's spending an innovation token wisely.

## Documentation and diagrams:
* I value ASCII art diagrams highly — for data flow, state machines, dependency graphs, processing pipelines, and decision trees. Use them liberally in plans and design docs.
* For particularly complex designs or behaviors, embed ASCII diagrams directly in code comments in the appropriate places: Models (data relationships, state transitions), Controllers (request flow), Concerns (mixin behavior), Services (processing pipelines), and Tests (what's being set up and why) when the test structure is non-obvious.

172	   - What can go wrong at each step? (null/undefined, invalid input, network failure, empty collection)
173	3. **Diagram the execution.** For each changed file, draw an ASCII diagram showing:
174	   - Every function/method that was added or modified
175	   - Every conditional branch (if/else, switch, ternary, guard clause, early return)
176	   - Every error path (try/catch, rescue, error boundary, fallback)
177	   - Every call to another function (trace into it — does IT have untested branches?)
178	   - Every edge: what happens with null input? Empty array? Invalid type?
179	
180	This is the critical step — you're building a map of every line of code that can execute differently based on input. Every branch in this diagram needs a test.
181	
182	**Step 2. Map user flows, interactions, and error states:**
183	
184	Code coverage isn't enough — you need to cover how real users interact with the changed code. For each changed feature, think through:
185	
186	- **User flows:** What sequence of actions does a user take that touches this code? Map the full journey (e.g., "user clicks 'Pay' → form validates → API call → success/failure screen"). Each step in the journey needs a test.
187	- **Interaction edge cases:** What happens when the user does something unexpected?
188	  - Double-click/rapid resubmit
189	  - Navigate away mid-operation (back button, close tab, click another link)
190	  - Submit with stale data (page sat open for 30 minutes, session expired)
191	  - Slow connection (API takes 10 seconds — what does the user see?)
192	  - Concurrent actions (two tabs, same form)
193	- **Error states the user can see:** For every error the code handles, what does the user actually experience?
194	  - Is there a clear error message or a silent failure?
195	  - Can the user recover (retry, go back, fix input) or are they stuck?
196	  - What happens with no network? With a 500 from the API? With invalid data from the server?
197	- **Empty/zero/boundary states:** What does the UI show with zero results? With 10,000 results? With a single character input? With maximum-length input?
198	
199	Add these to your diagram alongside the code branches. A user flow with no test is just as much a gap as an untested if/else.
200	
201	**Step 3. Check each branch against existing tests:**
202	
203	Go through your diagram branch by branch — both code paths AND user flows. For each one, search for a test that exercises it:
204	- Function `processPayment()` → look for `billing.test.ts`, `billing.spec.ts`, `test/billing_test.rb`
205	- An if/else → look for tests covering BOTH the true AND false path
206	- An error handler → look for a test that triggers that specific error condition
207	- A call to `helperFn()` that has its own branches → those branches need tests too
208	- A user flow → look for an integration or E2E test that walks through the journey
209	- An interaction edge case → look for a test that simulates the unexpected action

211	Quality scoring rubric:
212	- ★★★  Tests behavior with edge cases AND error paths
213	- ★★   Tests correct behavior, happy path only
214	- ★    Smoke test / existence check / trivial assertion (e.g., "it renders", "it doesn't throw")

216	### E2E Test Decision Matrix
217	
218	When checking each branch, also determine whether a unit test or E2E/integration test is the right tool:
219	
220	**RECOMMEND E2E (mark as [→E2E] in the diagram):**
221	- Common user flow spanning 3+ components/services (e.g., signup → verify email → first login)
222	- Integration point where mocking hides real failures (e.g., API → queue → worker → DB)
223	- Auth/payment/data-destruction flows — too important to trust unit tests alone
224	
225	**RECOMMEND EVAL (mark as [→EVAL] in the diagram):**
226	- Critical LLM call that needs a quality eval (e.g., prompt change → test output still meets quality bar)
227	- Changes to prompt templates, system instructions, or tool definitions

229	**STICK WITH UNIT TESTS:**
230	- Pure function with clear inputs/outputs
231	- Internal helper with no side effects
232	- Edge case of a single function (null input, empty array)
233	- Obscure/rare flow that isn't customer-facing

235	### REGRESSION RULE (mandatory)
236	
237	**IRON RULE:** When the coverage audit identifies a REGRESSION — code that previously worked but the diff broke — a regression test is added to the plan as a critical requirement. No AskUserQuestion. No skipping. Regressions are the highest-priority test because they prove something broke.
238	
239	A regression is when:
240	- The diff modifies existing behavior (not new code)
241	- The existing test suite (if any) doesn't cover the changed path
242	- The change introduces a new failure mode for existing callers
243	
244	When uncertain whether a change is a regression, err on the side of writing the test.

LEARNINGS: 10 loaded (5 pitfalls, 4 operationals, 1 pattern)

## Pitfalls
- [nonthrowing-continuation-publishes-killed-child] (confidence: 10/10, observed, 2026-08-05)
  StatusCommandRunner.run wraps a NON-throwing withCheckedContinuation in withTaskCancellationHandler, so a cancelled probe SIGKILLs the child and STILL RETURNS a normal-looking CommandResult (exitCode = signal number: 9 SIGKILL / 15 SIGTERM, timedOut false, stdout empty or truncated). Cancellation-safety therefore rests on ~13 call sites each remembering if Task.isCancelled after the await. refreshGitHubCLI forgot AND buried the write behind the await where no caller guard reaches, so classifyGitHubCLI read exit 9 as .notAuthenticated and the write stamped ghStatusCheckedAt, making the 60s TTL gate suppress every re-probe that would have healed it. Follow-ons: a TIMEOUT also sets signaled because terminate() is SIGTERM, so consumers must test timedOut BEFORE signaled; and VCSWriting.swift:1099 still prints git exited 15 because commit a64e4269 fixed this class only for WorkroomCLI.CLIResult, never for CommandResult. (files: macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift, macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift)
- [jj-at-sign-is-workspace-scoped-not-repo-global] (confidence: 10/10, cross-model, 2026-08-01)
  jj @ is WORKSPACE-scoped (resolved against the cwd), so any jj command using @ must run in the workroom, not the project root — even though bookmarks ARE repo-global. Running jj git push --change @ at the project root published the ROOT workspace working copy and left the selected workroom commit unpushed while returning success (verified jj 0.43). --bookmark works from a secondary workspace too, so nothing required the root. The integration test could not catch it because it passed the same directory as both path and projectRoot — any test of per-workroom placement must pass DIFFERENT values. (files: macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSWriting.swift)
- [argv-option-injection-via-remote-controlled-branch-name] (confidence: 10/10, cross-model, 2026-08-01)
  A repo-derived branch/remote name in a BARE argv slot is option injection even with no shell. The LOCAL branch name is not trusted input: refs/heads/--all is a legal refname (check-ref-format accepts the full refname; only --branch shorthand refuses) and a malicious remote pointing HEAD there makes git clone create a local branch named --all, which git branch --show-current reports. Verified git 2.55: push <remote> --all pushed EVERY branch in the repo; --mirror deletes remote refs. Critically `--` fixes push and fetch but NOT pull: git pull forwards the refspec to fetch in a way that still parses it as an option, so a --upload-pack=<script> branch name executed locally even with `--` present. 1	# Fix issue #146 — Investigate's untracked agent + diverging call sites
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Issue #146 found two bugs in the "Investigate" button (issue #49), which opens an interactive
6	`claude` session seeded with a failed command's context. It has two call sites —
7	`TerminalStatusBar.swift` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — and both call
8	`TerminalSessions.addRunTab` directly instead of going through `AppStore`, which violates
9	`addRunTab`'s own documented contract ("The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
10	`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab.").
11	
12	**Bug 1 (low severity):** because neither call site registers with `AppStore.runStates`, the
13	spawned agent is invisible to `hasLiveRunCommand`. Quit and window-close teardown never notice
14	it's alive — a live Investigate conversation gets silently SIGHUP'd instead of getting the same
15	"still running, are you sure?" treatment a run command gets. The issue's own severity note is
16	right that there's no port to leak, but silently killing an interactive session mid-conversation
17	is still a real (if minor) UX gap.
18	
19	**Bug 2 (medium severity, user-visible):** the tab-strip call site hardcodes the literal
20	`"claude"` instead of building the seeded prompt via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`
21	the way the status-bar site does. Opening Investigate from the tab-strip popover throws away the
22	whole point of the feature — the agent starts with no idea what failed.
23	
24	The chosen fix (confirmed with the user): don't widen `RunState`/`runStates` — that model is one
25	value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
26	(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
27	must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
28	Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
29	call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.
30	
31	## Changes
32	
33	### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point
34	
35	Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
36	`RunState`:
37	
38	```swift
39	/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
40	/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
41	/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
42	/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
43	/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
44	/// SIGHUP'ing it.
45	@Published private(set) var investigateTabs: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTarget.ID] = [:]
46	```
47	
48	Near `startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:~1916`), add the single entry point
49	both views will call:
50	
51	```swift
52	/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
53	/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
54	/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
55	@discardableResult
56	func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
57	  -> TerminalTab
58	{
59	  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
60	  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
61	  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
62	  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
63	    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
64	  }
65	  return tab
66	}
67	```
68	
69	Update `hasLiveRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:2257`) to also check live Investigate tabs, reusing
70	the same `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` pattern `liveRunView` already uses:
71	
72	```swift
73	var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
74	  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
75	    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
76	      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
77	    }
78	}
79	```
80	
81	In the `onTabsRemoved` closure (`AppStore.swift:916-941`), which already clears `runStates` when
82	its tab is closed/reaped, add the equivalent purge for `investigateTabs` so a closed tab's entry
83	doesn't linger:
84	
85	```swift
86	ids.forEach { self.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: $0) }
87	```
88	
89	Do **not** touch `gracefullyStopRuns`/`gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` — they SIGTERM a target's
90	run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session
91	has none of. `hasLiveRunCommand` going true is what makes `windowShouldClose`'s confirm-on-close
92	alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the
93	process on confirm is just the surface's normal teardown, same as closing any terminal tab.
94	
95	### 2. `TerminalStatusBar.swift:326-332` — route through the new method
96	
97	Replace the direct `addRunTab` call in the `onInvestigate` closure:
98	
99	```swift
100	onInvestigate: {
101	  let cwd = state?.view.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
102	  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: bannerState, target: target, cwd: cwd)
103	  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tabID)
104	  showingDiagnosis = false
105	},
106	```
107	
108	(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here.)
109	
110	### 3. `TerminalTabStrip.swift:436-441` — fix bug 2 and route through the new method
111	
112	Replace the hardcoded `"claude"` + direct `addRunTab` call:
113	
114	```swift
115	onInvestigate: {
116	  let cwd = tab.surface?.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
117	  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: state, target: target, cwd: cwd)
118	  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tab.id)
119	  agentPopoverTab = nil
120	},
121	```
122	
123	(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here; `state` is the `AgentBannerState`
124	already bound by the enclosing `if let state = agentManager.banners[tab.id]`. `tab.surface`
125	(`TerminalSessions.swift:33-36`) already collapses the `if case .terminal(let s) = tab.content`
126	match — no need to hand-roll it again, matching the status-bar site's `state?.view` shape.)
127	
128	This fixes bug 2 (both sites now build the identical seeded command via
129	`AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`) and closes bug 1 (both sites now go through
130	`AppStore`, which owns the tracking, restoring `addRunTab`'s documented caller contract).
131	
132	### 4. `TerminalSessions.swift:945-952` — doc note
133	
134	Add one line to `addRunTab`'s doc comment noting Investigate sessions are tracked in
135	`AppStore.investigateTabs`, not `runStates`, so the split is explicit at the definition too (not
136	just at the call sites) — closes the issue's "or a comment explaining why" fallback for the part
137	that *is* staying a deliberate design choice (no cross-window dedup, no supervisor/pidfile).
138	
139	## Verification
140	
141	- `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests.swift` — add:
142	  - A test asserting `startInvestigate` produces a tab whose command matches
143	    `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` for a given `AgentBannerState`, and that
144	    `investigateTabs[tab.id] == target.id` afterward — covers "both call sites build the same
145	    command line" (the issue's suggested unit check) by construction, since both now call the
146	    one method.
147	  - A test that `hasLiveRunCommand` is `false` before `startInvestigate`, `true` while the tab's
148	    surface reports a live process, and `false` again after simulating `onChildExited` and
149	    (separately) after simulating tab removal — two independent cleanup paths, both must be
150	    tested (mirrors the existing `testGracefullyStopAllWaitsForEveryLiveCommandThenCompletes` /
151	    `testReapClearsRunState` style already in this file).
152	  - A test that `gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` completes immediately (no hang) when the only
153	    live process is an Investigate tab and `runStates` is empty — this exact combination
154	    (`hasLiveRunCommand == true` via `investigateTabs`, but nothing in `runStates` to iterate) is
155	    new with this change; the existing `testGracefullyStopAllCompletesImmediatelyWhenNothingLive`
156	    only covers the "nothing at all is live" case.
157	- `make app-lint` / `make app-format` on the touched files.
158	- `make app-test` (or scoped `xcodebuild -only-testing:WorkroomAppTests/RunCommandTests`) green.
159	- Manual, per the issue's own verification section:
160	  - Fail a command, open Investigate from the status bar and from the tab-strip chip — confirm
161	    both agents start with the failure context (the prompt text, not a bare `claude`).
162	  - Start Investigate, then close the *window* (⌘W the window / red close button, not the tab)
163	    with "confirm on quit" enabled — confirm the close-confirmation now fires for the live agent
164	    instead of silently killing it. **Note:** ⌘Q (app quit) is intentionally NOT part of this
165	    check — `stopRunCommandsThenTerminate` (`WorkroomApp.swift:627-646`) shows no alert at all,
166	    for any live run command, and that's unchanged here: sending a stop signal to an interactive
167	    `claude` REPL and waiting for a "clean exit" has no defined meaning the way it does for a
168	    supervised dev-server (which traps SIGTERM to release a port) — extending quit-time
169	    protection to Investigate sessions is out of scope for this issue (see "NOT in scope" below).

## Failure modes

| Codepath | Realistic failure | Tested? | Error handling? | User-visible or silent? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `startInvestigate` → `addRunTab` | Surface fails to spawn (`tab.surface?.didSpawnFail`) | No | None added (matches Investigate's pre-existing behavior — never had spawn-failure handling) | **Visible** — the tab focuses immediately (unlike a backgrounded dev-server run), so the user sees the failure directly in the pane |

| Tab closes and process exits in the same tick | Both cleanup paths (`onChildExited` and `onTabsRemoved`) fire for the same tab id | No dedicated test, but `Dictionary.removeValue(forKey:)` on an absent key is a safe no-op | N/A — idempotent by construction | N/A |

- `TerminalSessions.addRunTab` — reused as-is; not modified beyond a doc-comment line.
- `AppStore.startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` — the existing pattern `startInvestigate` is

- `AppStore.liveRunView`'s `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` idiom — reused

  building a separate removal mechanism.
- `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` — already existed and was already correct; the bug

- `TerminalTab.surface` (`TerminalSessions.swift:33-36`) — reused in the `TerminalTabStrip` fix

questions.question: Correction: my earlier claim that "⌘Q shows no alert at all" was WRONG. WorkroomApp.swift:595-619 (applicationShouldTerminate) shows an UNCONDITIONAL "Quit Workroom? Quitting closes all terminals and stops any running processes." alert whenever confirmOnQuit is on (default), regardless of hasAnyLiveRunCommand — it already covers a live Investigate session today, no code change needed for that part. 1	# Fix issue #146 — Investigate's untracked agent + diverging call sites
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Issue #146 found two bugs in the "Investigate" button (issue #49), which opens an interactive
6	`claude` session seeded with a failed command's context. It has two call sites —
7	`TerminalStatusBar.swift` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — and both call
8	`TerminalSessions.addRunTab` directly instead of going through `AppStore`, which violates
9	`addRunTab`'s own documented contract ("The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
10	`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab.").
11	
12	**Bug 1 (low severity):** because neither call site registers with `AppStore.runStates`, the
13	spawned agent is invisible to `hasLiveRunCommand`. Quit and window-close teardown never notice
14	it's alive — a live Investigate conversation gets silently SIGHUP'd instead of getting the same
15	"still running, are you sure?" treatment a run command gets. The issue's own severity note is
16	right that there's no port to leak, but silently killing an interactive session mid-conversation
17	is still a real (if minor) UX gap.
18	
19	**Bug 2 (medium severity, user-visible):** the tab-strip call site hardcodes the literal
20	`"claude"` instead of building the seeded prompt via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`
21	the way the status-bar site does. Opening Investigate from the tab-strip popover throws away the
22	whole point of the feature — the agent starts with no idea what failed.
23	
24	The chosen fix (confirmed with the user): don't widen `RunState`/`runStates` — that model is one
25	value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
26	(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
27	must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
28	Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
29	call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.
30	
31	## Changes
32	
33	### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point
34	
35	Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
36	`RunState`:
37	
38	```swift
39	/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
40	/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
41	/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
42	/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
43	/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
44	/// SIGHUP'ing it.
45	///
46	///        runStates                    investigateTabs
47	///   [TargetID: RunState]          [TabID: TargetID]
48	///   one slot per target      many tabs allowed per target
49	///   (dev-server run)              (interactive claude)
50	///            │                            │
51	///            └─────────────┬──────────────┘
52	///                          ▼
53	///               hasLiveRunCommand (OR)
54	///                          │
55	///              ┌───────────┴────────────┐
56	///              ▼                        ▼
57	///   windowShouldClose confirm   stopRunCommandsThenTerminate (⌘Q)
58	///   alert — now fires for a     — unaffected in practice: only
59	///   live Investigate session    `runStates` feeds the actual
60	///                                gracefully-stop loop
61	@Published private(set) var investigateTabs: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTarget.ID] = [:]
62	```
63	
64	Near `startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:~1916`), add the single entry point
65	both views will call:
66	
67	```swift
68	/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
69	/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
70	/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
71	@discardableResult
72	func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
73	  -> TerminalTab
74	{
75	  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
76	  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
77	  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
78	  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
79	    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
80	  }
81	  return tab
82	}
83	```
84	
85	Update `hasLiveRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:2257`) to also check live Investigate tabs, reusing
86	the same `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` pattern `liveRunView` already uses:
87	
88	```swift
89	var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
90	  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
91	    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
92	      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
93	    }
94	}
95	```
96	
97	In the `onTabsRemoved` closure (`AppStore.swift:916-941`), which already clears `runStates` when
98	its tab is closed/reaped, add the equivalent purge for `investigateTabs` so a closed tab's entry
99	doesn't linger:
100	
101	```swift
102	ids.forEach { self.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: $0) }
103	```
104	
105	Do **not** touch `gracefullyStopRuns`/`gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` — they SIGTERM a target's
106	run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session
107	has none of. `hasLiveRunCommand` going true is what makes `windowShouldClose`'s confirm-on-close
108	alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the
109	process on confirm is just the surface's normal teardown, same as closing any terminal tab.
110	
111	### 2. `TerminalStatusBar.swift:326-332` — route through the new method

118	  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: bannerState, target: target, cwd: cwd)

THE PLAN:
# Fix issue #146 — Investigate's untracked agent + diverging call sites

## Context

Issue #146 found two bugs in the "Investigate" button (issue #49), which opens an interactive
`claude` session seeded with a failed command's context. It has two call sites —
`TerminalStatusBar.swift` and `TerminalTabStrip.swift` — and both call
`TerminalSessions.addRunTab` directly instead of going through `AppStore`, which violates
`addRunTab`'s own documented contract ("The caller (`AppStore`) owns the run-state and wires
`onChildExited`; this just creates and shows the tab.").

**Bug 1 (low severity):** because neither call site registers with `AppStore.runStates`, the
spawned agent is invisible to `hasLiveRunCommand`. Quit and window-close teardown never notice
it's alive — a live Investigate conversation gets silently SIGHUP'd instead of getting the same
"still running, are you sure?" treatment a run command gets. The issue's own severity note is
right that there's no port to leak, but silently killing an interactive session mid-conversation
is still a real (if minor) UX gap.

**Bug 2 (medium severity, user-visible):** the tab-strip call site hardcodes the literal
`"claude"` instead of building the seeded prompt via `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)`
the way the status-bar site does. Opening Investigate from the tab-strip popover throws away the
whole point of the feature — the agent starts with no idea what failed.

The chosen fix (confirmed with the user): don't widen `RunState`/`runStates` — that model is one
value per *target*, for a dev-server-style run, and already has code that special-cases it
(`WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a target's run command across windows; an Investigate session
must **not** be deduped that way, two windows investigating the same target concurrently is fine).
Instead give Investigate its own small, separate ownership record in `AppStore`, and route both
call sites through one new `AppStore` method so they can't diverge again.

## Changes

### 1. `AppStore.swift` — new tracking + shared entry point

Near `runStates` (`AppStore.swift:1371`), add a sibling dictionary, deliberately not merged into
`RunState`:

```swift
/// Live Investigate sessions (issue #49/#146), tab → target. Kept separate from `runStates` (one
/// `RunState` per target, modelling a single dev-server-style run): an Investigate session is a
/// second, independent process that can coexist with a target's real run command, and must NOT be
/// deduped across windows the way `WindowRegistry.runOwner` dedupes a run command. Only feeds
/// `hasLiveRunCommand`, so quit/window-close notice a live agent conversation instead of silently
/// SIGHUP'ing it.
///
///        runStates                    investigateTabs
///   [TargetID: RunState]          [TabID: TargetID]
///   one slot per target      many tabs allowed per target
///   (dev-server run)              (interactive claude)
///            │                            │
///            └─────────────┬──────────────┘
///                          ▼
///               hasLiveRunCommand (OR)
///                          │
///              ┌───────────┴────────────┐
///              ▼                        ▼
///   windowShouldClose confirm   stopRunCommandsThenTerminate (⌘Q)
///   alert — now fires for a     — unaffected in practice: only
///   live Investigate session    `runStates` feeds the actual
///                                gracefully-stop loop
@Published private(set) var investigateTabs: [TerminalTab.ID: TerminalTarget.ID] = [:]
```

Near `startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:~1916`), add the single entry point
both views will call:

```swift
/// Start an interactive Investigate session (issue #49) seeded with the failure captured in
/// `bannerState`, in `cwd`. The one caller of `addRunTab` for Investigate (issue #146) — tracks the
/// tab in `investigateTabs` so it isn't invisible to quit/close teardown.
@discardableResult
func startInvestigate(bannerState: AgentBannerState, target: TerminalTarget, cwd: String)
  -> TerminalTab
{
  let command = AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for: bannerState)
  let tab = terminals.addRunTab(for: target, command: command, cwd: cwd)
  investigateTabs[tab.id] = target.id
  tab.surface?.onChildExited = { [weak self] _ in
    self?.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: tab.id)
  }
  return tab
}
```

Update `hasLiveRunCommand` (`AppStore.swift:2257`) to also check live Investigate tabs, reusing
the same `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` pattern `liveRunView` already uses:

```swift
var hasLiveRunCommand: Bool {
  runStates.keys.contains { liveRunView(for: $0) != nil }
    || investigateTabs.contains { tabID, targetID in
      terminals.view(forTab: tabID, inTarget: targetID)?.hasLiveProcess ?? false
    }
}
```

In the `onTabsRemoved` closure (`AppStore.swift:916-941`), which already clears `runStates` when
its tab is closed/reaped, add the equivalent purge for `investigateTabs` so a closed tab's entry
doesn't linger:

```swift
ids.forEach { self.investigateTabs.removeValue(forKey: $0) }
```

Do **not** touch `gracefullyStopRuns`/`gracefullyStopAllRunCommands` — they SIGTERM a target's
run-command *supervisor* (the `wait_after_command` pidfile wrapper), which an Investigate session
has none of. `hasLiveRunCommand` going true is what makes `windowShouldClose`'s confirm-on-close
alert fire for a live Investigate session (`WindowRegistry.swift:241-269`); actually stopping the
process on confirm is just the surface's normal teardown, same as closing any terminal tab.

### 2. `TerminalStatusBar.swift:326-332` — route through the new method

Replace the direct `addRunTab` call in the `onInvestigate` closure:

```swift
onInvestigate: {
  let cwd = state?.view.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: bannerState, target: target, cwd: cwd)
  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tabID)
  showingDiagnosis = false
},
```

(`store: AppStore` is already an `@EnvironmentObject` here.)

### 3. `TerminalTabStrip.swift:436-441` — fix bug 2 and route through the new method

Replace the hardcoded `"claude"` + direct `addRunTab` call:

```swift
onInvestigate: {
  let cwd = tab.surface?.lastKnownCwd ?? target.path
  _ = store.startInvestigate(bannerState: state, target: target, cwd: cwd)
  agentManager.dismiss(tab: tab.id)
  agentPopoverTab = nil
},

## What already exists

- `TerminalSessions.addRunTab` — reused as-is; not modified beyond a doc-comment line.
- `AppStore.startRunCommand`/`respawnRunCommand` — the existing pattern `startInvestigate` is
  modeled on (create tab → wire `onChildExited` → track ownership).
- `AppStore.liveRunView`'s `terminals.view(forTab:inTarget:)` + `hasLiveProcess` idiom — reused
  verbatim inside the new `hasLiveRunCommand` clause instead of inventing a second way to ask
  "is this tab's process alive."
- `onTabsRemoved`'s existing `runStates` purge block — extended with a sibling line rather than
  building a separate removal mechanism.
- `AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` — already existed and was already correct; the bug
  was that one call site never called it.
- `TerminalTab.surface` (`TerminalSessions.swift:33-36`) — reused in the `TerminalTabStrip` fix
  instead of re-deriving the same pattern-match a third time in the codebase.

Nothing in this plan rebuilds a flow that already exists — every new line either reuses an
established accessor/pattern or is genuinely new bookkeeping (`investigateTabs` itself, which has
no existing equivalent since Investigate was previously untracked entirely).

## NOT in scope

- **Widening `RunState`/`runStates` to support multiple tabs per target.** Rejected in favor of a
  separate `investigateTabs` record (see Context) — `RunState` and `WindowRegistry.runOwner` are
  purpose-built for a single dev-server-style run per target, and an Investigate session must not
  inherit that single-slot/cross-window-dedup semantics.
- **Sending a live Investigate tab a graceful stop signal on quit** (mirroring how
  `gracefullyStopRuns` Ctrl-C's-and-waits for a dev-server run command). Discussed and rejected —
  quit already shows an unconditional "stops any running processes" confirm alert regardless of
  what's running (`WorkroomApp.swift:595-619`, not gated on `hasAnyLiveRunCommand`), and a killed
  Investigate session is resumable next launch via the existing `AgentResumeCoordinator`
  (`claude --resume`). Sending a stop signal and waiting for a "clean exit" also has no defined
  meaning for an interactive REPL the way it does for a dev server releasing a port. Not logged as
  a TODO — the user-facing concern is already soft-landed twice over (blanket dialog + resume).
- **Cross-window dedup for Investigate sessions.** `WindowRegistry.runOwner` deliberately continues
  to see only `runStates` — two windows investigating the same target concurrently is intended
  behavior, not a gap.
- **Spawn-failure handling (outcome/toast) for a failed Investigate launch.** Investigate never had
  this; adding it now would be scope creep beyond what issue #146 asked for, and the failure is
  already visible to the user (see Failure modes).

## Worktree parallelization strategy

Sequential implementation, no parallelization opportunity — every change centers on the single new
`AppStore.startInvestigate` method and its two call sites; the `TerminalSessions.swift` doc line
and the test file are small enough that splitting them into separate worktrees would cost more in
coordination than it saves.
